questions.solution_html:
• Why is water considered as universal solvent? [U]/
  • [CO2,CO3]
  • Water is called the universal solvent because it can dissolve a wider variety of substances than
  • any other solvent. This is due to its unique polar molecular structure, where the positive and
  • negative ends of water molecules can attract and pull apart other molecules or ions, allowing
  • them to be dissolved.

questions.question: Explain the role of dairy products as functional foods. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of dairy products as functional foods. [U] [CO3, CO4]
  • Health benefits of dairy as functional foods
  • • Digestive health: Fermented dairy products like yogurt, kefir, and some cheeses contain
  • probiotics that support gut health and can improve digestive function.
  • • Bone health: Dairy is a rich source of highly absorbable calcium, protein, phosphorus,
  • and vitamin D, all essential for building and maintaining strong bones and potentially
  • preventing osteoporosis.
  • • Cardiovascular health: Certain compounds in dairy, like bioactive peptides found in
  • fermented milk and whey, have been shown to help lower blood pressure and reduce the
  • absorption of cholesterol.
  • • Immune support: Dairy products and their components, like whey proteins, can have
  • immunomodulatory effects, helping to regulate immune responses and potentially
  • reducing inflammation

questions.question: Explain the significance of mineral balance in the body and how deficiencies or excess can affect health / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of mineral balance in the body and how deficiencies or excess can
  • affect health. [U] [CO2,CO3]
  • Significance of mineral balance
  • • Structural Support: Minerals like calcium are essential for building and maintaining
  • strong bones and teeth.
  • • Nerve and Muscle Function: Minerals facilitate nerve signal transmission and muscle
  • contractions.
  • • Fluid and Electrolyte Balance: Minerals such as sodium, potassium, and chloride are
  • electrolytes that help regulate the body's fluid balance and blood pressure.
  • Health consequences of deficiency
  • • Osteoporosis: Long-term calcium deficiency can lead to decreased bone density, which
  • can progress to osteoporosis.
  • • Anemia: Iron deficiency can cause anemia, a condition where the blood can't carry
  • enough oxygen to the body's tissues.
  • • Impaired Immune Function: Deficiencies in minerals like zinc can lead to a weaker
  • immune system, making you more susceptible to illness
